operationalization: C = C_m, M = observed baryons, alpha = 1 (option 2)
evidence_class: preregistered observational falsification test; not blind
implementation_notes: x_scale is not specified by the preregistration; it was fixed before running to the natural parameter scales (0.1 dex, sigma_fD, sigma_i, max(V_obs)^2, 0.5 dex).
The halo radius uses the catalogue radius; the free r_c absorbs distance rescaling.
interpretation: Under both nuisance treatments, the SPARC rotation curves require mass beyond the observed baryons, so Candidate A with M = observed baryons, C = C_m and alpha = 1 is falsified for disc galaxies.
Calling the missing mass 'emergent matter' would be a relabelling unless Candidate A independently predicted its amount and distribution.
This tests one assistant-proposed operationalization of Candidate A (option 2), pending Kirk LaSalle's confirmation.
It is not blind: the mass discrepancy in SPARC was known in the literature and in this repository before the preregistration was frozen.
Option 1 (M = all gravitating energy) is an exact GR identity and is not tested here.
